steps: Extend the index finger of your dominant hand, keeping the other fingers folded away.
Raise the fingertip to your face, near the cheek or the side of the nose.
Brush the fingertip downward in one smooth stroke, ending below the cheek.
Keep your palm facing inward toward your own face through the brush.
Pair the sign with a neutral expression, mouthing 'pink' as you sign it.
tip: Cheek or nose both occur — colour signs vary by region in the UK, so match your local signers.

steps: Hold both hands open and flat in front of your torso, fingers together.
Touch the middle fingertips of both hands lightly against your chest.
Drag both hands slowly upward across your chest without lifting them away.
Keep your palms facing inward toward your body for the whole movement.
Mirror the feeling with your face — soft and open for good feelings, tense for bad ones.
tip: Emotions live on the face in BSL — the upward drag means little without the expression to match.

steps: Close both hands into fists, leaving both thumbs extended and loose.
Press the knuckles of both fists together in front of your heart.
Push both hands a short distance forward, away from your chest.
Keep the thumbs pointing upward and relaxed through the movement.
Smile gently and mouth 'kind' — the warm face carries the meaning.
tip: Think of two fists offering goodness forward from the heart.

steps: Close your dominant hand into a fist, extending only the thumb upward.
Raise the fist to your face, placing the thumb tip against your chin.
Drag the thumb tip once across your chin, from your non-dominant side.
Keep the thumb angled upward and your palm facing inward through the stroke.
Smile as you sign — a flat expression can read as 'tidy' or 'clean' instead.
tip: One stroke across the chin with the thumb — 'Nice' lives at the jawline.

steps: Form a 'V' with your dominant index and middle fingers, folding the rest away.
Raise the hand up beside your eye, keeping the fingertips pointing upward.
Push the V handshape straight forward, away from your face.
Turn your palm to face yourself, keeping the fingers vertical through the push.
Look along your hand as it moves, so your gaze follows the 'seeing' direction.
tip: The two fingers stand for your eyes — the push shows the gaze travelling out.

steps: Hold both hands as flat blades, fingers together and straight, thumbs tucked.
Rest the flat edge of your dominant hand across the top of the other hand.
Tap the bottom edge of the upper hand against the top edge of the lower hand.
Keep both palms facing sideways, fingertips pointing across your body.
Repeat the small tapping motion twice, keeping your expression businesslike.
tip: One flat hand stacked on the other — like layers of effort piling up.

steps: Extend the index finger of your dominant hand, folding the others away.
Raise the fingertip to the side of your forehead, near the temple.
Tap the side of your head once or twice with the fingertip.
Keep your palm facing inward and the finger pointing at the head.
Hold a thoughtful expression — the sign needs the 'thinking' face to land.
tip: Tapping the head shows thoughts happening inside — one or two taps is enough.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand open and flat, palm up, fingertips pointing forward.
Close your dominant hand into a fist, leaving the thumb extended.
Swipe the extended thumb sharply downward across the open palm.
Keep the open hand steady as the base while the thumb does the work.
Use a decisive expression — the firm swipe marks the beginning of something.
tip: The thumb 'switches on' against the flat hand — one crisp downward swipe.

steps: Hold both hands open and flat in front of your body, fingers together.
Turn both palms to face upward, as if holding two invisible balls.
Circle both hands continuously, the left going one way and the right the other.
Keep the circles small and even, just above waist height.
Smile — play is joyful, and a stiff face reads as mechanical.
tip: Two hands circling in opposite directions — nothing else in the dictionary moves quite like it.

steps: Close both hands into tight fists, keeping the thumbs tucked inside.
Hold both fists in front of your chest at shoulder width.
Pump the fists up and down in quick alternation, like pumping arms while running.
Keep the fists vertical, moving about a hand's length with each pump.
Lean your body slightly forward — the lean sells the running motion.
tip: Your fists become the pumping arms of a runner — alternate fast and short.
